$comment: The shape rules the no-real-names hook checks a staged file against: what a name looks
like, and what stands a name-shaped pair down (a place, a job title, a reserved domain,
the inside of a uuid). Each rule was learned by an exception, and each exception used to
be a code change. Now it is a line here, and the hook says which section cleared a pair
(`NAMES_WHY=1`, or `--why`), so the next one is a data change with a known section.
This file is DATA. No code lives here, so a non-Python host can read it directly.
Every name in this file is a word, never a person.

why.place_first: A gazetteer and a geocoder's tests quote pairs like a direction and a state, or a saint's-name city: name-shaped, and places. A first word here stands the pair down. Learned 2026-09-01 from a gazetteer.
why.place_last: The same gazetteer, the other way round: a river, a county, a bay area, a kingdom. A last word here (trailing punctuation stripped) stands the pair down. Learned 2026-09-01 from a gazetteer.
why.role_last: A role catalogue is a page of two- and three-word job titles, every one name-shaped. A last word here stands the pair down. Learned 2026-09-01 from a role catalogue.
why.shapes_off: A catalogue of event names (an all-hands, a hack week, a party) is name-shaped and no list will ever know every shape, so a file carrying the marker in its first lines turns the shape rule off for itself -- and only the shape rule: a name from the graph is still refused there. Data files with these suffixes are off by the same token: a gazetteer's towns are quoted proper nouns and none are people. Learned 2026-09-01 via the file marker.
why.reserved_domains: RFC 2606 / 6761 reserve these so that nobody can be reached at them, which is exactly why tests use them. An entry without a dot is a top-level label and matches any domain ending in it; an entry with a dot matches the whole domain only. Learned 2026-09-01 from RFC 2606.
why.not_a_contact: A mailbox nobody reads is not a person's contact. An address containing one of these is not reported.
why.patterns: uuid: the middle of one holds digits and dashes at a phone number's length, so a phone-shaped run inside a uuid stands down (learned 2026-09-01 from a Teams id). nameish: a Name-shaped run of one to four words inside a quoted string; a surname may be one letter, because a person with one passed straight through when two were demanded.
why.skip_suffixes: Files the hook never reads: images, weights, lockfiles and minified bundles, where a match is noise and the read is slow.
